# openobserve_folder (Resource)

Manages a folder that groups dashboards, alerts, reports, synthetics, or downtimes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openobserve_folder" "platform_dashboards" {
  name        = "Platform"
  description = "Dashboards owned by the platform team"
}

resource "openobserve_folder" "platform_alerts" {
  folder_type = "alerts"
  name        = "Platform"
  description = "Alerts owned by the platform team"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Folder name, unique within the organization and folder type.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form folder description.
- `folder_type` (String) What the folder holds: `dashboards` (default), `alerts`, `reports`, `synthetics`, or `downtimes`. Downtime folders need OpenObserve Enterprise v1.2.0-rc1 or later.
- `icon` (String) Icon the UI shows beside the folder name: a Unicode emoji such as `"🚀"`, or an OpenObserve icon reference such as `"o2:redis"`. The server stores it as written and does not check it.

Leave it unset to keep whatever icon the folder has, so one picked in the UI is not removed by an unrelated change. Set it to manage the icon, and a change made elsewhere then shows as drift. Set it to `""` to remove the icon. Needs OpenObserve v1.0.0 or later: an older server drops the icon, which the provider reports as a warning on create and an error on update.
- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `folder_id` (String) Server-assigned folder identifier. Reference this from dashboards and alerts.
- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{folder_type}/{folder_id}`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Folders are imported as {org_id}/{folder_type}/{folder_id}.
terraform import openobserve_folder.platform_dashboards default/dashboards/7123abcdef
```
